findings.title: The report's containment check is a second copy of assertContained and already disagrees with it
findings.recommendation: Design D1 says the report runs 'the same real-path test the emit surface's assertContained runs', and its own rationale for moving findArchivedDir is that two copies of one rule are two rules waiting to diverge (R-crc-14). The containment test was copied rather than shared, and the copies differ at one edge: isInsideArchive returns false when the entry's real path IS the archive root (real !== realRoot is required), while assertContained (src/core/emit-composition.ts:690) accepts that case as contained. So an archive entry `2026-01-01-foo -> .` is refused by the report with the message 'resolves outside orbit/changes/archive', which is false, while orbit emit archive and the address-reviews fallback accept the same entry and write into the archive root's .orbit-runs/. Repair: make one exported predicate the single statement of the rule (e.g. isInsideArchive's body generalised to isContained(dir, root, {allowRoot})) and have assertContained call it, then decide once whether the root itself counts as contained. Or, if the stricter reading is the one you want, apply it to the emit surface's archived scope too and correct D1's 'same test' sentence.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: One shared containment predicate used by both assertContained and the report; settle the root-equality case once (refusing it is the safer reading for an archived scope).

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Keep two functions but make them agree, add a test pinning the root-equality case on both surfaces, and reword design D1 so it no longer claims the same test.

findings.reproduction: In a scratch project: mkdir -p orbit/changes/archive && ln -s . orbit/changes/archive/2026-01-01-foo. findArchivedDir(root,'foo') returns the entry (statSync says directory); isInsideArchive(root, entry) returns false; `orbit status --change foo --report` prints 'Error: archived change 'foo' resolves outside orbit/changes/archive — a symlinked archive entry is not a renderable trail'. By reading assertContained's condition (throw only when real !== realRoot && !real.startsWith(realRoot + sep)), the emit surface accepts the same entry: real === realRoot does not throw.

commentary: Probed by running the built CLI against all 49 archived changes in this repository rather than trusting the fixtures: 41 render, 5 fail at the pre-capability boundary (b3 through d2), 3 have no review pass at all. That run is also the evidence for task 4.1 (rc10-apply-closure renders its newest pass, a verification, ending at `Archived: orbit/changes/archive/2026-10-11-rc10-apply-closure`), though the task's disposition is the archive step's to record. The miss error, the read-only claim and the active-wins order were spot-checked from the CLI as well. Historical paths inside rendered findings still read orbit/changes/<name>/... because they are the record's own text, not composed by the renderer; that is correct and needs no change. Pass 0 ran as direct checks (task state, `orbit validate --strict`, the scenario map at 24 of 24 declared, the four touched suites at 108 green) rather than through the verify skill. Passes 4 and 5 are skipped because orbit/lenses/ does not exist. Pass 6 ran as a scoped residue sweep over the change's vocabulary (findArchivedDir, validateChangeExists, the Q-crc-26 wording), not as the full audit-drift scan; the only residue is Q-crc-26 still open in the program doc, which at-archive note 4.2 already owns.

direction.reasoning: The change does what it says on the real repository: every archived change at or past the D4 boundary now renders with the Archived: tail, the five pre-D4 archives fail with the pre-capability error by design, and the three oldest have no renderable pass. The active path is untouched, the resolver move is clean, and the new scenarios are each exercised by a CLI-level test. The one defect is small and at a degenerate edge, but it is the exact shape the change's own D1 warns against, so it is worth fixing before archive rather than carrying as a residual.
